proposals.before: Yet at lunar culmination the horizontal parallax is smallest while true motion is slowest, which would make the separation distance larger.
proposals.after: Yet when the Moon is at apogee the horizontal parallax is smallest while true motion is slowest, which would make the separation distance larger.
proposals.reason: Chinese 最高 in this lunar-parallax and true-motion context means apogee, not meridian culmination; the idiomatic rendering invents the wrong astronomical term.

proposals.before: When the Moon's southern latitude exceeds 60° of quadrant distance, or northern latitude exceeds 70°, apply the following procedure.
proposals.after: When the Moon is in southern latitude and its quadrant distance exceeds 60°, or in northern latitude with quadrant distance exceeding 70°, apply the following procedure.
proposals.reason: The Chinese separately states lunar latitude side (緯南/緯北) and quadrant-distance thresholds (月距限過六十/七十度); the idiomatic fuses them into “southern latitude exceeds 60° of quadrant distance,” which misstates the condition.

decisions.reason: s0077 places the Moon 在最高時 with 地半徑差最小 and 月實行必遲. Smallest horizontal parallax and slowest true motion mark lunar apogee, not meridian culmination; 'at apogee' restores the orbital sense of 最高.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 月在最高時，地半徑差最小，而其月實行必遲

decisions.reason: s0144 states two paired conditions: 月在緯南 with 月距限過六十度, and 月在緯北 with 月距限過七十度. The prior idiomatic fuses latitude side into the degree threshold; the proposed wording keeps latitude side and quadrant-distance limits separate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 月在緯南，月距限過六十度，及月在緯北，月距限過七十度
